name: MonarchKbd
title: Kbd
summary: A keyboard key or shortcut drawn as a key cap, such as Ctrl+K or ⌘K. By default it is drawn only while a hardware keyboard is attached.
whenToUse: Beside a menu item, a button or a search field to show its keyboard shortcut to people who use a hardware keyboard, on tablets, Chromebooks and desktop windows.
whenNotToUse: For code in running text use MonarchInlineCodeStyle. For a shortcut that only exists on the web, show nothing.
api: @Composable fun MonarchKbd(keys: String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, alwaysVisible: Boolean = false, labels: MonarchKbdLabels = MonarchKbdLabels())

class MonarchKbdLabels(command: String? = null, shift: String? = null, option: String? = null, control: String? = null, returnKey: String? = null, escape: String? = null, delete: String? = null, tab: String? = null, space: String? = null, capsLock: String? = null, upArrow: String? = null, downArrow: String? = null, leftArrow: String? = null, rightArrow: String? = null)

options.name: keys
options.description: The key or shortcut as it is shown, such as "Esc", "Ctrl+K" or "⇧⌘P".

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the component. Not applied while the cap is hidden.

options.name: alwaysVisible
options.description: Draw the cap without a hardware keyboard too.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the names TalkBack reads for the key glyphs ⌘ ⇧ ⌥ ⌃ ↩ ⎋ ⌫ ⇥ ␣ ⇪ ↑ ↓ ← → (monarch_kbd_command and the others).

states.name: keyboard attached
states.description: Configuration.keyboard is KEYBOARD_QWERTY and the keyboard is not hidden: the cap is drawn.

states.name: no keyboard
states.description: Nothing is drawn and the component takes no room, unless alwaysVisible is true. The configuration changes when a keyboard is attached or detached, so the cap appears and disappears.

appearance: A key cap with 4dp corners on the subtle background, a default border with a thicker bottom edge, and the keys in muted text in the code typeface, in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web Kbd is always visible, because a browser cannot tell whether a keyboard is present; on Android, as on iOS, the hint is hidden on a device without one. The web text is 11px; Android uses the code role (14sp) because smaller text is not legible on a phone. The spoken key names are an addition shared with iOS: a browser leaves the glyphs to the screen reader. iOS calls the flag isAlwaysVisible and the label return; Kotlin uses alwaysVisible and returnKey because return is a keyword.
accessibility: The cap is one TalkBack element whose content description names the keys: "⇧⌘P" is read as "Shift Command P".
Characters that are not key glyphs are read as written, so "Esc" and "Ctrl+K" are unchanged.
The text grows with the font size setting and the smallest size of the cap grows with it.
The cap is not interactive and has no click action.
The key is shown by a border and a shape, not by color alone.
edgeCases: Whether a keyboard is attached comes from LocalConfiguration: keyboard is KEYBOARD_QWERTY and hardKeyboardHidden is not HARDKEYBOARDHIDDEN_YES. A 12-key keypad does not count.
Emulators often report a QWERTY keyboard, so the cap shows there.
Long text wraps inside the cap.
An empty string draws an empty cap of the smallest size.
